answer.origin: NVIDIA Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR) dated and filed August 17, 2026, with Items 1.01, 2.03 and 7.01 and a furnished press release (Exhibit 99.1). Primary source for NVIDIA's own statement; no independent corroboration in the supplied records.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own 8-K states that on August 17, 2026 it entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as Lessor, covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site (PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio), with an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC as tenant. NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation for the initial commitment is capped at $105 billion, payable only if OpenAI defaults through insolvency or non-payment and the lease shortfall is not recovered, and only after the Lessor meets ready-for-service conditions expected from 2028. NVIDIA also holds an option to add credit support for about 3.8 GW more at its sole discretion, which is not a committed obligation. OpenAI agreed to reimburse amounts NVIDIA actually pays. On the stated terms, the source supports a conditional read that NVIDIA is taking on contingent, large-scale credit exposure to secure AI data center capacity for a single tenant, so its financial risk depends mainly on OpenAI's credit and on the lease economics, neither of which is disclosed here. This rests on the 8-K summary; the full agreements are not yet public.
limitations: The full text of the Agreements is not in the supplied records; the 8-K says it will be filed as an exhibit to the 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, so the guaranteed minimum values, lease terms and termination mechanics are known only from the summary.
The guaranteed minimum value per lease and the fee or pricing NVIDIA receives, if any, are not disclosed, so the expected loss and the economics of the guaranty cannot be estimated.
Whether the $105 billion cap is ever reached, and how much NVIDIA would actually pay, depends on an OpenAI default and on recoveries from replacement leases or sale, none of which is disclosed.
The 3.8 GW additional credit support is at NVIDIA's sole discretion and has no disclosed amount or timing, so it is not a committed obligation.
The ready-for-service date is only 'expected beginning in 2028'; the timing of any payment is therefore uncertain.

The press release (Exhibit 99.1) and the Lessor's and OpenAI's own disclosures are not in the supplied records, so the stated partnership benefits and OpenAI's credit standing are not independently verified.
Whether NVIDIA will record a liability or only disclose the guaranty depends on accounting treatment that is not described in the source.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, for the filed Agreements exhibit and any guaranteed minimum value, lease-term and termination details.
Check the press release in Exhibit 99.1 for any stated economics, OpenAI commitments and expected capacity schedule.
Check NVIDIA's next annual report on Form 10-K for disclosure of the guaranty amount, any liability recognized, and the status of the ready-for-service conditions.
Check whether any subsequent 8-K reports lease commencements, ready-for-service milestones, or exercise of the additional 3.8 GW credit support.
Check OpenAI's and the Lessor's public statements and credit ratings for any change in the tenant's ability to pay, since that drives the trigger.

proposal.question: Will NVIDIA's next annual Form 10-K disclose the SB Energy residual value guaranties with a stated maximum or recognized exposure tied to the $105 billion initial cap, or disclose a recognized liability for them?
proposal.settled_by: NVIDIA's next annual report on Form 10-K (fiscal year after the year ended January 2026) disclosure of the guaranties, including any stated maximum exposure, recognized liability or contingent-liability note referencing the SB Energy Agreements.
proposal.time_scope: Next annual filing: the Form 10-K covering the current fiscal year, expected around early 2027.
proposal.lost_if_folded: Folding this into a general NVIDIA or AI capacity question would lose the specific measure of how much contingent credit exposure NVIDIA has accepted for one tenant's leases, and whether its own annual disclosure quantifies the $105 billion cap.
